newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends up on China talk, soymeal falls.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends up on China talk, soymeal falls.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed higher on Monday, supported by ideas China may be in the market for U.S. soyoil, and on unwinding of soyoil/soymeal spreads, traders said.
USDA last week confirmed China bought 20,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil and Singapore traders said China bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal.

Soymeal futures fell sharply on fund long liquidation and on unwinding of spreads as traders bought soyoil and sold soymeal, pit sources said. October soymeal led the declines, falling $4.70 per ton ahead of expiry Tuesday.
Commercial and fund short covering also boosted soyoil futures. Merrill Lynch reportedly bought 1,000 lots December and 200 lots January on the day, traders said.
Cargill was said to be a buyer of December soyoil late. Iowa Grain and Smith Barney were also said to be active in the December and January.
Commercials were noted buyers of soymeal with ADM, Central Soya, Continental Grain and Produce Grain buyers of the December and October, traders said.
Rand Financial, Merrill Lynch and Harris Futures Corp were said to be sellers, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated at 1,600 lots while soyoil was pegged at 1,700 lots, CBOT reported.
